questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go on exchange in a country where English was the official language.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My exchange was amazing! the only  con is the expensive accomodation.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy enough and I could just email KU or UCD if I had any questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: at the orientation week we met the student organization that would help us throughout our exchange as well as the UCD global team.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was difficult due to the housing crisis. I found mine through a facebook group. Most of the other exchange students lived with hostfamilies

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in Ranelagh and I really liked it, but as it is difficult to find off campus accommodation, I would recommend living on campus if they have enough rooms available.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not get accommodation on campus because they do not have enough rooms for all the exchange students, and it is quite difficult to find accommodation.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Applying at UCD was fine but registering for courses was more difficult, as the module might be full, but the school administration helped me and registered me for the modules and lab practicals that I wanted.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: UCD sends out a registration form, where you write the modules you want to register + a back-up module. UCD will email you with the modules that they registered for, if any of the modules were full they will ask you to select other modules (unless you get in contact with the administration).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The office at the science department helped me register for all my modules.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The school administration contacted the module coordinator to register me for the modules that I did not get, The email I got previously informed me, that some of the modules were full capacity, so I ended up getting all my modules as the module coordinator agreed to let me register in their module.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would advise future students to contact the school administration in the science department if they have any problems with module registration.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The professors are mostly researchers, so it is interesting to learn more about their research and new  experimental strategies and technology they used to conduct their research

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is easier at UCD than in Copenhagen. The lectures are helpful, and the lab practicals give a better understanding of the subject in practise.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching is the same. I would say that at UCPH the lectures help understand the chapters we study in the books, whereas the lectures at UCD is more of an "Everything you need to know" of the topics.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I enrolled in Toxicology, Molecular basis of disease and molecular pharmacology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Toxicology was nice since there is no exam, so there is enough time to study the other subjects. I also found molecular pharmacology very interesting and helpful with regard to my bachelor project.  Molecular basis of disease was also a good course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: My phone subscription ran out of EU data (Oister), so the data of my last 20 day was taxed and is very expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Local transportation is very cheap, and some specific groceries are much cheaper compared to Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a great selection of clubs, and it is cheap to be enrolled in the extracurricular activities. I wanted to be a member of the hiking club, so I could explore Ireland while meeting new people, but unfortunately the club was full.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are everything you can think of really. Information of all the clubs and activities can be seen at UCD website.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely the hiking club as you will get a unique opportunity t explore Ireland with other students, and they rent a bus to take you to the destination and back to UCD again, a bonus since public transport takes a long time.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hike in Bray, Howth, ring of Kerry in Killarney and Wicklow national park. The view is spectacular!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: the population in Dublin is very international, so it is easy to blend in.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Local students love pubs. There is also a pub at UCD where you can meet alot of both local and international students and get a cheap beer.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really, they are very easy-going.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Most people were really nice and went out of their way to help you with directions etc.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Make sure data will be covered during your exchange in those 4 months.
2. Find accommodation and select courses at UCPH in case you do not find accommodation, and if you do, you can cancel the courses at UCPH.
3. Explore Ireland :-D

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to check your email, as the email for on-campus accommodation will be sent out a day before you can apply, and due to housing crisis on-campus accommodation is in high demand.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends I gained during my semester

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding accomodation.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
